title: Order reversal transports coherent adjunction data
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, internal functor simplicial sets and coherent comma categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], coherent adjunction data of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data], and the opposite simplicial sets and mapping-space comparisons of [lem-coef-infinity-op-mapping-reversal]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $R:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be coherent functors equipped with coherent adjunction data $L\dashv R$, with unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\to RL$, counit $\epsilon:LR\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B}$, both specified triangle $2$-simplices, and the specified initial and terminal universal-arrow conditions. Then order reversal transports these data to coherent adjunction data $R^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv L^{\mathrm{op}}$. The new unit is $\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}}\to L^{\mathrm{op}}R^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the new counit is $\eta^{\mathrm{op}}:R^{\mathrm{op}}L^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Under the canonical isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}),$$
the reversed original right triangle is the new left triangle and the reversed original left triangle is the new right triangle. For every $a\in\mathcal A$ and $b\in\mathcal B$ the canonical isomorphisms
$$(a\downarrow R)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(R^{\mathrm{op}}\downarrow a),\qquad(L\downarrow b)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(b\downarrow L^{\mathrm{op}})$$
carry $(La,\eta_a)$ to the terminal universal arrow for the reversed counit and $(Rb,\epsilon_b)$ to the initial universal arrow for the reversed unit. These identifications retain all simplices of the unit, counit and triangle diagrams and commute with restriction of their parameter simplices. Applying reversal twice returns the original data.

source.place: Definition 6.2.1.1 (02EK), the two triangle conditions, together with Construction 1.4.2.2 and Remarks 1.4.2.3 and 1.4.2.7 (003L), order reversal. Agent-formulated transport of the specified coherent adjunction data and universal comma objects. Read online 2026-10-17, not archived; these are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: For a simplicial set $X$, reverse every simplex by the operator $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^\vee$. The defining identities $(\beta\alpha)^\vee=\beta^\vee\alpha^\vee$ and $(\alpha^\vee)^\vee=\alpha$ make this an involutive functor on simplicial sets and on simplicial maps. Applying the same reversal in the diagram and parameter factors gives canonical involutive identifications of the internal functor simplicial sets with the opposites of the functor categories displayed in the statement. The opposite of $L$ (respectively $R$) therefore has source and target $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$ (respectively $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$). The composition and identity classes, and all their coherent witnesses, are carried to reversed ones by [lem-coef-infinity-op-mapping-reversal].

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2 and Remarks 1.4.2.3–1.4.2.7; reversal in both diagram and parameter factors

proof.text: Reverse the specified unit and counit simplices. Since reversal exchanges the endpoints of every edge, $\eta:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\to RL$ becomes $\eta^{\mathrm{op}}:R^{\mathrm{op}}L^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}}$, while $\epsilon:LR\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B}$ becomes $\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}}\to L^{\mathrm{op}}R^{\mathrm{op}}$. Thus these are respectively the counit and unit required for $R^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv L^{\mathrm{op}}$. Naturality under simplicial functors and preservation of all parameter simplices follow from the composition-compatible reversal in [lem-coef-infinity-op-mapping-reversal].

source.place: Definition 6.2.1.1 and order reversal of the unit and counit

proof.text: The original right triangle is the specified $2$-simplex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)$ with successive edges $\eta R$ and $R\epsilon$ and degenerate long edge at $R$; reversing its simplex and using the second canonical functor identification gives a $2$-simplex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}})$ whose vertices are those of the original in reverse order, so its first edge is the reversal of $R\epsilon$ and its second edge the reversal of $\eta R$. Since the identification commutes with pre- and postcomposition by functors, these are $R^{\mathrm{op}}\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}:R^{\mathrm{op}}\to R^{\mathrm{op}}L^{\mathrm{op}}R^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\eta^{\mathrm{op}}R^{\mathrm{op}}:R^{\mathrm{op}}L^{\mathrm{op}}R^{\mathrm{op}}\to R^{\mathrm{op}}$, with long edge still degenerate at $R^{\mathrm{op}}$. For the new left adjoint $R^{\mathrm{op}}$, unit $\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}$ and counit $\eta^{\mathrm{op}}$, this is exactly the left triangle. Similarly the original left triangle in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$, with edges $L\eta$ and $\epsilon L$, reverses to the $2$-simplex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}})$ with successive edges $\epsilon^{\mathrm{op}}L^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $L^{\mathrm{op}}\eta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and degenerate long edge at $L^{\mathrm{op}}$: the right triangle for the new right adjoint $L^{\mathrm{op}}$. The triangle-witness clause of [lem-coef-infinity-op-mapping-reversal] ensures this is an identification of the specified higher simplices, not merely an equality in a homotopy category.

source.place: the two triangle conditions in Definition 6.2.1.1, transported through Construction 1.4.2.2

proof.text: Unfold the coherent comma categories as the simplicial pullbacks in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Reversing both the object and arrow simplices in that pullback gives natural isomorphisms $(a\downarrow R)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(R^{\mathrm{op}}\downarrow a)$ and $(L\downarrow b)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(b\downarrow L^{\mathrm{op}})$, including all parameter simplices and their compatibility homotopies. Under the first isomorphism the initial object $(La,\eta_a)$ becomes terminal with arrow $\eta_a^{\mathrm{op}}$; under the second, the terminal object $(Rb,\epsilon_b)$ becomes initial with arrow $\epsilon_b^{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence the reversed unit and counit satisfy exactly the initial and terminal universal-arrow clauses of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data].

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2 and Remarks 1.4.2.3, 1.4.2.7; reversal of comma pullbacks

proof.text: The preceding constructions use the literal simplex-reversal operator, so they commute with restriction along every parameter simplex and preserve all faces and degeneracies. Applying reversal a second time uses $(\alpha^\vee)^\vee=\alpha$ and returns $L,R,\eta,\epsilon$, both triangle witnesses, and both comma universal arrows on the nose under the displayed canonical identifications. Therefore the transported data are coherent adjunction data $R^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv L^{\mathrm{op}}$, and opposite twice is the original data.

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2 and Remark 1.4.2.7, involutivity and restriction compatibility

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NH-4af075399 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 5 steps and the three cited statements in full: def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones (Fun, the comma pullbacks, initial and terminal objects), def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data (orientations, triangle edges L eta, eps L and eta R, R eps, and the universal arrows) and lem-coef-infinity-op-mapping-reversal (X^op, Map_{C^op}(x,y) ~ Map_C(y,x), and its composition, identity and witness compatibility). I also read the citer's step 4 in lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion, which takes L -| F^op to F -| L^op; the statement gives exactly that. The statement is correct and not weakened. The new adjunction is R^op -| L^op with unit eps^op and counit eta^op. (a|R)^op = (R^op|a) holds because Fun(Delta^1,A)^op = Fun(Delta^1,A^op) with ev0 and ev1 swapped. Initial becomes terminal through the statement of the mapping-space reversal. The reversed right triangle has edges R^op eps^op then eta^op R^op, which is the new left triangle. I tested Delta^0, [1] with the identity adjunction, empty A, and nerves of ordinary categories (matching the classical op adjunction). Fault E3/E4: step 3 named the reversed edges 'eps^op R^op' and 'R^op eta^op', which are ill-typed under the definition's whiskering convention and in the wrong order. I rewrote it with the vertex order and the correct edges for both triangles. B4: step 1 had '$alpha' for '$\alpha'; fixed. Only the proof text changed: no new nodes, no change to the statement or dependencies, no tool_uses. The route stays in the same unit plus one definition, and no SGA is cited. No duplicate found by rg over dag/nodes. The Kerodon sources 02EK and 003L are not archived (the report lists them as WANTED), and proof_origin is correctly 'agent'.
